articles.title: 'Show me one damaged vehicle': Nitin Gadkari's dare on ethanol blending, targets vested interests
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday talked about the Centre's ethanol-blending programme, rejecting claims that mixing ethanol with petrol
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday talked about the Centre's ethanol-blending programme, rejecting claims that mixing ethanol with petrol damages vehicles and arguing that the policy has also opened a new avenue for farmers to diversify beyond food production.Speaking at the inaugural session of the Bihar Investor Summit 2026, Gadkari said millions of vehicles had already been operating on ethanol-blended petrol since 2022 without, in his account, widespread complaints of damage."I challenge anybody to come up with the complaint that his or her vehicle has suffered damage on this account. Of course, those with vested interests may have some other story to tell," said Gadkari, who holds portfolios of Road Transport and Highways, as quoted by PTI.Gadkari said the policy was designed not merely to reduce dependence on conventional fuel but also to create an additional market for agricultural produce. "We must understand that the decision to blend ethanol with petrol was taken with a view to diversification of agriculture towards energy and power sectors... Our farmers shall no longer remain 'anna data' (food producers) but also become 'urja data' (energy producers)," he said.According to Gadkari, about 4 crore four-wheelers and 20 crore two-wheelers have been running on petrol blended with ethanol since 2022. He also claimed that major automobile manufacturers had tested vehicles using higher ethanol blends, including 100% ethanol."Of course, we are importing (conventional fuel) worth Rs 22 lakh crore, and those who feel that their business will get hit are bound to feel bad. But let me tell you, I am the minister in charge of the department concerned; all leading automobile brands have tried running their vehicles even on 100 per cent ethanol. And there have been no complaints," he said.The minister also linked ethanol production to higher farm incomes, saying the use of corn for ethanol had generated additional earnings for farmers in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh."After the Union government took the decision to make ethanol out of corn and the same was used for the aforementioned purposes, it resulted in additional earnings of up to Rs 45,000 crore for farmers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Is it not preferable to serve the interests of those from whom we import (fuel)," he asked.Gadkari cited other examples of efforts to develop alternative fuels, including aviation fuel made using agricultural waste. "We have even made aviation fuel with rice straw. The future belongs to innovation, technology and research. And a state like Bihar has to play a key role in this direction," he said.Turning to Bihar's investment potential, Gadkari said the state could expand its economic base through sectors such as tourism. He also pointed to international demand for makhana, a crop widely produced in the state.He described Bihar as having significant economic potential and praised Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's leadership."Under the leadership of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the state is bound to scale new heights," he said.Meanwhile, Choudhary, addressing the summit, appealed to investors to set up businesses in Bihar and assured them of access to a large market if their products met the required standards.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Gavin Newsom orders California firms to keep 'AI' name unchanged after Trump's 'superintelligence' decree
articles.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has taken another swipe at President Donald Trump, this time over the administration’s push to replace the term
articles.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom has taken another swipe at President Donald Trump, this time over the administration’s push to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “superintelligence”.Newsom on Wednesday signed an executive order directing California state agencies and departments under his authority to continue referring to the technology as “artificial intelligence” or “AI”, regardless of any different terminology adopted by the federal government, unless required otherwise by law.Sharing the move on X, Newsom said: “I just signed an executive order permanently declaring Artificial Intelligence ‘Artificial Intelligence’ in California. You’re welcome, America.”The order states that California agencies must refer to artificial intelligence as “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI”, even if the federal government adopts different or rebranded terminology.Newsom hits back at Trump’s ‘superintelligence’ pushThe order came a day after Trump directed the federal government to use the term “superintelligence” for AI, arguing that the technology is “not artificial”.Newsom, in a statement accompanying his executive order, said: “Super intelligence is clearly not coming from the White House — that’s why California continues to lead.”The California governor has also criticised what he described as a lack of federal action on AI safety. Speaking to reporters, Newsom said, “We have to do a lot more in the absence of federal leadership,” while leaving open the possibility of calling lawmakers back for a special session on the issue.Newsom’s executive order also argues that changing the terminology for AI should not distract from addressing documented safety and security risks associated with the technology.His announcement also came alongside the signing of several California bills aimed at protecting workers from potential AI-related impacts, including measures concerning layoff notices and restrictions on using AI in disciplinary and firing decisions.Trump gets tech CEOs to back ‘Super Intelligence’ termTrump’s push to rebrand AI followed a White House meeting with several leading technology executives on Tuesday.Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signed the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence” during the meeting.The accord encourages AI companies to monitor the capabilities of their models and establish internal teams to help prevent AI systems from carrying out unintended hacks.The document, however, drew attention for a typo under Trump’s signature, where the United States was referred to as the “Unites States.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Jagtar Singh Johal: Scot detained in India freed on bail after nine years in prison
articles.summary: The Sikh activist from Dumbarton was arrested in 2017 in connection with alleged terror offences.
articles.body:
A Scottish Sikh activist has been released from prison in India after being detained for almost nine years without being convicted.

Jagtar Singh Johal, from Dumbarton, was arrested in 2017 in connection with alleged terror offences.

The Indian authorities have accused the 39-year-old of having a role in a series of targeted killings of religious and political figures - allegations which he denies.

Johal was granted bail at Delhi High Court on 18 September, but has only now been released from detention.

He had to surrender his passport as part of his bail conditions and is barred from speaking to the media about the case.

Johal was arrested in the Punjab region in 2017, just weeks after his wedding in the country.

He is accused of travelling to Paris in 2013 and handing about £3,000 to the Khalistan Liberation Force – an armed organisation which has carried out violent attacks in pursuit of a separate Sikh state.

It is claimed that this money was used to fund weapons to kill, or attempt to kill, religious and political figures in Punjab in 2016 and 2017.

The Indian authorities claim Johal is a member of the KLF and that "he actively participated and had complete knowledge of the conspiracy".

However, his supporters say he was targeted for blogging about alleged human rights abuses against the Sikh community in India and was coerced into signing a false confession to participation in the killings.

Johal's family say no concrete evidence has been presented against him and that the case was built on the testimony of unreliable witnesses.

His imprisonment was recognised by a UN panel as arbitrary detention in 2022 and he has claimed to have been tortured.

Indian authorities have previously denied the torture claim and have repeatedly maintained due process is being followed.

Last year Johal was acquitted in a case where he was accused of financially supporting the KLF terror group.

He remained in prison because he faces federal charges in eight other cases, for which he potentially faces the death penalty.

However, his legal team argues that these cases are almost identical and that the other charges should be dismissed.

There have been hundreds of hearings over the past nine years and the bail order concludes that the trial is "certainly not likely to conclude anytime soon".

His brother Gurpreet Singh Johal - who has lobbied successive governments calling for his release - said the decision to grant bail had been a "really important milestone".

"It is just a first step, but it is a step in the right direction," he said.

The move was also welcomed by politicians and the legal charities Redress and Reprieve, who represent Johal in the UK.

Reprieve's deputy executive director Dan Dolan said the release was "a really important moment" - but that Johal still faced the death penalty on "trumped up charges".

"It is really important that we recognise he's not out of the woods yet," he said.

"We now really need to push to get him home."

Redress said Johal's release from prison could not undo "the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention".

articles.title: ED arrests two accused in Rs 1,417cr investment fraud case
articles.summary: CHENNAI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested two men in connection with an alleged ₹1,417.86 crore investment fraud linked to Unique Exports and
articles.body: CHENNAI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested two men in connection with an alleged ₹1,417.86 crore investment fraud linked to Unique Exports and its associated entities, with the agency alleging that funds collected from thousands of investors were routed through a network of more than 100 bank accounts and disguised as business expenses.The ED's Chennai Zonal Office-II arrested S Naveen Kumar and S Muthuselvam on Sept 29 under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. They were produced before the Special Court for PMLA cases, which remanded both in judicial custody.The money-laundering investigation followed an FIR registered by the district crime branch, Erode, under various provisions of the IPC and the Tamil Nadu Protection of Interests of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act (TNPID Act).According to the ED, Naveen Kumar, Muthuselvam and their associates devised and operated investment schemes named UNI, FNP, FAP and UNR under the banner of Unique Exports, East Valley Agro Firms and other related entities. Investors were allegedly lured with promises of high returns from exports of agricultural commodities.The investigation, however, revealed that Unique Exports and its associated entities did not undertake substantial export activities but continued to collect money from investors on the promise of returns generated through export profits, the ED said.The agency's investigation has so far found that approximately ₹1,417.86 crore was mobilised from around 35,759 investors. Of this, about ₹719 crore was found deposited in bank accounts of entities linked to Unique Exports. The investor funds were allegedly routed through more than 100 bank accounts held in the names of Unique Exports, associated concerns, family members and close associates.The ED identified Naveen Kumar, proprietor of Unique Exports, as the alleged mastermind behind the investment schemes. According to the agency, he controlled the banking operations and movement of investor funds.Banking analysis allegedly showed that around ₹390.90 crore was recorded as salary payments, despite only four persons working in the concern. Another ₹79.56 crore was recorded as payments for onion and commodity purchases, although no actual purchase of agricultural goods was found. articles.title: Fugitive postmaster arrested after two years
articles.summary: Kendrapada postmaster Dipankar Das arrested after two years for allegedly misappropriating Rs 30 lakh from 100+ customers’ postal scheme accounts.
articles.body: Kendrapada: A 46-year-old fugitive postmaster, who had allegedly misappropriated around Rs 30 lakh from the accounts of more than 100 customers at a post office in Kendrapada district, was arrested on Wednesday night after evading police for over two years.Dipankar Das, postmaster of the post office at Krushnanagar village under Talachua Marine police station limits, had been absconding since June 2024. Police registered a case against him for allegedly siphoning off over Rs 30 lakh deposited by customers in various postal schemes.The irregularities came to light in June 2024 when some depositors discovered that money had been illegally withdrawn from several passbooks. Police said Das allegedly doctored their signatures to make the withdrawals. He also allegedly embezzled money by failing to enter deposits in postal ledgers, while recording the transactions in customers’ passbooks. Most of those who lost their hard-earned money are fishermen, housewives, farmers and small businessmen. After the irregularities were detected, a senior postal official of Pattamundai sub-divisional post office suspended Das and lodged an FIR against him.“Acting on the FIR, we filed a case against the accused in Talachua police station under various of IPC. He fled from his village after the police filed a case against him. Acting on a tip-off, we arrested him on Wednesday night from Krushnanagar, as he came to attend a family function,” said IIC of Talachua marine police station, Biswabhusan Sahani, adding, “The accused was produced in the court at Rajnagar on Thursday. articles.title: New liquor shops in Bengal must maintain 500-metre gap from schools, religious places
articles.summary: The West Bengal government has increased the necessary distance for new retail liquor outlets from educational institutions and holy places to 500 meters
articles.body: The West Bengal government has increased the necessary distance for new retail liquor outlets from educational institutions and holy places to 500 meters in urban and municipal areas and 1 km in other parts of the state, up from the former 300 meters, as per PTI.As per the recent notification given by the government, no new liquor licenses would be given within a 1 km distance of religious institutions, schools, and universities in rural and non-municipal areas, state Liquor Association Secretary Bijan Patra stated on Thursday.The government has kept the minimum distance at 500 meters from the religious places, schools, and educational insititutions for the areas under the Kolkata Municipal corporation (KMC) and other civic authorities, Bijan Patra added.However, he stated that Rule 8's distance requirements won't apply if an existing liquor store wishes to "shift" to a mall of any size.The prior framework required a minimum distance of 1,000 feet, or around 300 meters.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari had already announced that his administration will not enable liquor sales within a 1 km radius of schools, universities, and shrines.Over 4,000 bars, off-shops, and liquor stores now operate within a 1-kilometer radius of these sensitive zones throughout the state; however, this new restriction will not affect already-existing establishments.In order to establish new offshops through bars, the new strategy also makes use of Section 4P of the excise act.However, some business owners have voiced reservations about the provision, claiming that because the state agency would keep a profit, it could not be advantageous for the liquor sector.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Comando: 7-kg Chihuahua joins Mexico’s National Guard; trains for search-and-rescue work and appears at public events
articles.summary: A Chihuahua named Comando has become one of the most unusual members of Mexico’s National Guard.
articles.body: A Chihuahua named Comando has become one of the most unusual members of Mexico’s National Guard. At 13 months old, the 7-kilogram dog is the smallest canine recruit in a force that has about 350 dogs, most of them much larger working breeds such as German Shepherds and Labradors. Comando has been fitted with miniature goggles, a tactical vest, a helmet and a small camera mounted on his head. The Chihuahua is being trained for search-and-rescue work, while also taking on a very visible role at ceremonies, school events and community programmes. His small size has made him an unexpected public face of the National Guard, with appearances that have also drawn attention on social media.Who is Comando, the Chihuahua recruited by Mexico’s National Guard?Comando was adopted by Mexico’s National Guard about six months before Reuters reported on him in September 2026. He was taken in from the northern state of Chihuahua after his elderly owners could no longer care for him. The state where he was adopted also inspired his name.At 21 centimetres tall, Comando looks very different from the dogs normally associated with military and police units. Reuters reported that the Chihuahua is being trained for search-and-rescue work, alongside his appearances in public-facing activities.During a training session at a military base in Mexico City, Comando climbed stairs and moved over obstacles while a much larger, fully trained canine named Roko watched nearby.Comando has his own miniature tactical gearThe tiny recruit has been equipped with gear normally associated with much larger working dogs. Comando, on the other hand, wears miniature goggles, a fitted tactical vest and a helmet, along with a small camera mounted on his head.The equipment has become part of his distinctive appearance as he trains with the National Guard. Despite his size, officers are preparing him for search-and-rescue work rather than treating him solely as a ceremonial mascot.His training also puts him alongside the National Guard’s much larger canine recruits. The force has about 350 dogs, with German Shepherds and Labrador Retrievers among the more traditional working breeds. Comando, by contrast, is a Chihuahua with a height of just 21 centimetres and a weight of 7 kilograms.From National Guard ceremonies to social media memesComando’s role extends beyond training. He has appeared at civic ceremonies, school events and community outreach programmes, and he also took part in Mexico’s Independence Day parade.His unusual appearance has helped turn him into a recognisable public figure for the force. Comando has inspired an animated likeness and a growing number of memes on social media.Lieutenant Debora Hernandez via Reuters said Comando challenges the idea that only large dogs can serve in the National Guard. She also described his public role as a way of showing a more human side of uniformed personnel.For now, Comando remains a small recruit with an unusual combination of responsibilities, training for search-and-rescue work while appearing at public events as one of the National Guard’s most distinctive canine faces.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mullin tells Ruthless podcast that the Trump administration has apprehended 2,210 terrorists
articles.summary: Markwayne Mullin told the "Ruthless Podcast" that President Donald Trump shifted border security from defense to offense, aggressively pursuing terrorists nationwide.
articles.body: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told the "Ruthless Podcast" that 2,210 terrorists have been apprehended under the Trump administration’s aggressive approach to solving illegal immigration. "Underneath President Trump, we’ve arrested, so far as my numbers walking into here, 2,210 terrorists in this country," Mullin said in an exclusive interview released Thursday morning. "Most of them came over and claimed asylum, gave a fake name. Some of them we caught, but a lot of them came in and … the Biden administration was just cutting them loose." Mullin said that under the Biden administration, 97% of individuals DHS encountered were released within 27 hours. Earlier this month, ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, DHS had announced that it had detained 2,150 known or suspected terrorists. TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94% Mullin noted that these individuals were classified as terrorists. "There's a difference between a suspected terrorist and a terrorist watch list," the secretary explained to the co-hosts. "These were terrorists." Mullin said the arrests resulted from a new administration-wide approach to illegal immigration. "One directive we had is we're no longer just playing defense," Mullin told the hosts. "We're on the offense. President Trump has given us the authority to go on the offensive. For instance, cybersecurity. We're no longer sitting there and just protecting as you try to attack us. We're swimming upstream now. We're going after the people that are coming after us. We're aggressively going after individuals. I want to put you on offense." Mullin rose quickly to the Cabinet post. He served in the House before winning election to the Senate in 2022. President Donald Trump nominated him to lead DHS in March, and the Senate confirmed him 54-45 on March 23. I'm not joking when I say this. I haven't slept through the night in six months," the Oklahoman added. With just over a month to go until the November midterm elections, podcast co-host Josh Holmes commended the secretary for his job performance as immigration remains a polarizing political issue. "You also inherited a department that the reason it was shut down is that Democrats have demagogued everything to do with border security and ICE in particular," Holmes told Mullin. "Under the previous DHS administration, there was some kind of prioritization of the lowest-hanging fruit of deportations rather than what you're talking about, which is that people need to get the hell out of here as fast as possible."
